about: Moybyte's app and OS calls, one row each, and every tier's name for them (docs/os_2026-11/tiers.md section 1). moy-spec's game verbs are not here (the moy wasm module, libmoy), nor WASI's imports, which keep WASI's names. tools/gen_os_table.py writes every tier's table from this, and tests/test_os_table.py holds each to it. ROLES: the app ABI's roles in order (a grant's mask is 1 << role); grant is the permission that hands the role to a user app, never, or floor (every grant holds it); ctx whether an AppContext builds an object for it (runtime/shell/app_context.py); doc its line in docs/app_api_v1.md. ROWS: name is <role>.<verb> for a row of the role table (the ROLE door names it by its index among those rows, native/moy_app/moy_app.h: a row a role's server serves, or any row with door true), the POSIX name of a POSIX row, or the name of a kernel or Python row. kind is posix (POSIX's, its types its C prototype's) or moybyte (the default). server: c (native/moy_app's C), shell (the Python console's server for the role, runtime/shell/shell_servers.py), proc:<name> (the process moybyte.<name>'s), call (a console call: the moybyte module's function run as the calling process), kernel (the ELF kernel's own, native/moy_elf/moy_os.c), python (a name the Python console hands its programs). perm the permission a row answers under beyond its role's grant: the one that hands it to an app, or a gate its server passes (the front's, runtime/system/front.py); a list where several do. in the parameters in a neutral notation, name:type, type int (a 32-bit number), str (UTF-8 text), str? (text, empty or NULL for none), bytes, cart (a cart named by its folder) or out (a buffer the call writes, with its capacity); ret what the 32-bit answer is: int (the answer) or len (the length of what was written into the out); a negative answer is an error. how: hop (run on the VM's task), seq (read where it is called, under the app ABI's seqlock) or direct (the toolkit's own native). The tiers' projections: wasm true where a compiled app imports it from moybyte.app as <role>_<verb> (its WAMR signature from in, an out handed to the door's Python half as its capacity); wasi true where a WASI program imports it from moybyte.os as <verb> for a moybyte row, else <role>_<verb> (each text, buffer or bytes of its C prototype, or of its in, a pointer and a length, native/moy_wasm/moy_wasi_os_rows.h): the kernel serves a row with c, a moybyte row without one, not served in C and held by a Python name, is a console call posted on the VM's queue and answered by the scheduler's _CALLS (a call row by its verb, a Python row by its verb's message half, moybyte.<verb>_message, whose wake posts the program a message), and a C row (the moybyte role's crypto rows among them) or a call row no Python name holds (the device handles') is its role table row run for the program's app run (native/moy_wasm/moy_wasi.c, THE APP ROWS); elf its ordinal in the OS function table, or deferred (rows are appended, never changed, moved or removed: a row that goes is RETIRED, keeps its slot and answers through a typed stub, and version counts the ordinals; a moybyte row the door serves is named moy_<role>_<verb>, a console call moy_<verb>, its C prototype from in); lua and py the names a Lua and a Python program hold it by (Lua's are Python's, verbatim, a role an AppContext builds being Python's as ctx.<role>.<verb> and Lua's as <role>.<verb>; a Lua app and a Lua service hold the same names); door true where the door's Python half decodes its fields (DOOR_ARGS). A POSIX or kernel row's ELF details, and a moybyte row's whose compiled face the kernel serves itself (its c prototype names its C function): c its prototype exactly as the module's C library headers declare it (hdr) or as sdk/include/moybyte/os.h does; va, on a row whose prototype ends in ..., the one argument the kernel takes in its place and when; glibc the name glibc's headers use (the host's modules); fail what a retired row's stub answers (errno ENOSYS), null for a function that returns nothing; noreturn; u, on an ELF row with a prototype that takes a pointer, the rule each parameter is checked by before a U-mode module's call runs (tools/gen_os_table.py's U_TOKEN; a door row's comes from its in); retired the date and the reason. PERMISSIONS: the permission table (docs/os_2026-11/processes.md section 2): perm the manifest name (files also matches files:<folder>); grants floor, role:<role>, api:<service>, boot, lease, full_access or marker; prompt its line of the install prompt, full, or null; needs the console service it needs; py the names a Python program holds while it is granted, each None while Settings turns it off; doc what the app holds, its cell of docs/app_api_v1.md section 6's table (consecutive rows that say the same and serve the same tiers share one line); spec true where moy-spec's verbs serve it too; tiers only where no row serves it (a native module's run, a service's start). Every other permission's tiers are derived: the floor every tier, a marker Python, and else the tiers that serve its rows (and moy-spec's, for spec), so an install prompt never lists what the tier cannot do.

roles.doc: whole-surface invalidation: repaint next frame, or ask for one more frame from inside `draw()`; the kernel's flags, folded by the frame gate where it folds the console's dirty flag

the grant's surface row, which the shell writes wherever it changes (on the desk, the window the app is in): the canvas the app draws on, its size, its scales, the window flag, the content rect the host's exitable strip leaves a running app (`content_rect()`, `(x, y, w, h)`, and `bar_h()`, its `y` -- what a user app's ungated `content_rect()` and `bar_h()` read), the pointer in the surface's coordinates (`x`, `y`, `down`, `click`, `visible`). A glyph is `ui`'s (`ui.glyph`), not this role's

the live token table the look writes at every switch, under a generation: the token dict (rebuilt only when the generation moves), one token by its role id, the generation, the light flag, the theme's and variant's names (the reads every app is given, the floor); the verbs that change the look; and the Appearance page's (`docs/history/theming_2026-09.md` §9 phase 6 step 7): a change to the theme (landing in `custom`), what its rows show, CHROME SIZE, EDIT FILE, and NAME… (step 8: `custom` renamed into a theme of its own, and why a name will not do)

the USER-FILES store (#108), C rows over the layer in `native/moy_store/moy_ufiles.h`: named documents (`docs` is plain Markdown — `files/Documents/<name>.md`, the file's body IS the document), the trash, history sidecars, the image, cover and text codecs, provenance stamps; a grant made for a shared folder (a user app's) reaches the kinds in that folder alone
the CART store: the live cart list, a new cart, a project's undo journal and its images
where the console goes next: another app, the Editor, a document, a run
per-app settings on `system/settings`' rows, namespaced per app (the grant's namespace), a write saved as it is made

the console's own badges and every game's, as Settings lists them: one of the console's awarded by its id, the badges by game (each found one's day, each goal's last value), and today's date on the bar's clock as the badges record it

the desktop backdrop, the theme's (`docs/theme_and_shell_2026-11.md` D6): what is shown, the wallpaper carts, a wallpaper's title, a pick (a change to the theme, landing in `custom`; None is NONE, the theme's `desktop` fill), the live preview, My Art's thumbnail, and Paint's picture as Paint and Files copy a drawing into it (its two rows C, over the user-files layer), which a My Art pick copies into the theme
Paint's open picture, Paint's settings rows: which it is (`(kind, name)`, or None), and following it when its file is renamed under it
the system cut/copy/paste buffer (#132): at most 4 KiB of text, kernel state, so it outlives a VM stop; a longer `put_text` answers False and keeps the old text

carts from outside (#124): the network Get Carts fetches through, its radio lease, one store op of an install (`op(fn)`, inside the bus gate), the engine's sizing, this console's chip and compiled-code format; in the browser, the keeper that makes an install durable in OPFS, the page's file picker, and where carts come from on a page a board serves; the Wi-Fi page Get Carts opens when the radio has no network, and whether it is still open; the console's consent records, which the install prompt reads and writes (`runtime/shell/app_perms.py`)
